lessons.title: જો …, તો … (jo …, to …) — if, then
lessons.gloss: if you have a fever, then … — jo opens the condition, to opens what follows

segments.text: Say "if", then "if … then", from A2. (જો, જો … તો ….) Then "you should rest". (tamāre ārām karvo joīe.)
જો તમને તાવ છે, તો તમારે આરામ કરવો જોઈએ. jo tamne tāv che, to tamāre ārām karvo joīe. — "If you have a fever, then you should rest."

જો (jo) opens the condition, and તો (to), "then", opens what follows from it. Each half is a whole sentence with its own verb. In quick speech તો can drop, but written down it marks where the second half begins.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: if it is so now

segments.text: જો તમને ભૂખ છે, તો ખાઈ લો. jo tamne bhūkh che, to khāī lo. — "If you're hungry, then go ahead and eat."

When the condition is about now, it takes the present: જો તમને ભૂખ છે, જો તે ઘરે છે. The second half can be advice, a request with -ઓ, or a plain statement: જો ઠંડી છે, તો હું ઘરે રહીશ (jo ṭhanḍī che, to hũ ghare rahīś).

acceptedResponses: jo tamne tāv che, to tamāre dāktar pāse javũ joīe

feedback.correct: jo for the condition, to for the advice.

segments.text: Which word opens the condition? (જો.) Which opens the second half? (તો.) "If you have a fever"? (જો તમને તાવ છે.)

lessons.title: જો વરસાદ પડશે, તો … (jo varsād paḍśe, to …) — if it happens
lessons.gloss: if it rains, … — a condition about later takes the future, or the past when it would come first

segments.text: Say "if you have a fever, then you should rest". (jo tamne tāv che, to tamāre ārām karvo joīe.) Then "we will stay". (ame rahīśũ.)

blocks.title: Grammar Lens: the future after જો

segments.text: જો વરસાદ પડશે, તો અમે ઘરે રહીશું. jo varsād paḍśe, to ame ghare rahīśũ. — "If it rains, we'll stay at home."

English says "if it rains"; Gujarati says "if it will rain": a condition about later takes the future, પડશે, and so does the result, રહીશું. "If it doesn't rain" is the નહીં form: જો વરસાદ નહીં પડે, તો અમે જઈશું (jo varsād nahī̃ paḍe, to ame jaīśũ).

blocks.title: You'll want to know: the past after જો

segments.text: જો ટ્રેન છૂટી ગઈ, તો હું બસમાં આવીશ. jo ṭren chūṭī gaī, to hũ basmā̃ āvīś. — "If I miss the train, I'll come by bus."

When the condition would be over before the result starts, it can take the plain past: "if the train has gone, then …". જો મારું પાકીટ ખોવાઈ ગયું, તો હું પોલીસમાં ફરિયાદ કરીશ (jo mārũ pākīṭ khovāī gayũ, to hũ polīsmā̃ phariyād karīś).

segments.prompt: Say: if it rains, we'll stay at home; and if I miss the train, I'll come by bus.
acceptedResponses: jo varsād paḍśe, to ame ghare rahīśũ; jo ṭren chūṭī gaī, to hũ basmā̃ āvīś
જો વરસાદ પડશે, તો અમે ઘરે રહીશું. જો ટ્રેન છૂટી ગઈ, તો હું બસમાં આવીશ.
jo varsād paḍśe, to ame ghare rahīśũ. jo ṭren chūṭī gaī, to hũ basmā̃ āvīś.

feedback.correct: paḍśe, the future, for later; chūṭī gaī, the past, for what comes first.
feedback.incorrect: After jo, use the future for later: varsād paḍśe. For the missed train, the past: ṭren chūṭī gaī.

segments.text: "If it rains"? (જો વરસાદ પડશે.) "If it doesn't rain"? (જો વરસાદ નહીં પડે.) "If I miss the train"? (જો ટ્રેન છૂટી ગઈ.)
Before the new one: say "if it rains, we'll stay at home". (jo varsād paḍśe, to ame ghare rahīśũ.) Then "quickly" and "an umbrella". (જલદી, છત્રી.)
નહીંતર — nahī̃tar — "otherwise; or else". First what to do, then નહીંતર, then what will happen if it is not done:
જલદી ચાલો, નહીંતર ટ્રેન છૂટી જશે. jaldī cālo, nahī̃tar ṭren chūṭī jaśe. — "Walk quickly, or else we'll miss the train."
છત્રી લો, નહીંતર તમે પલળી જશો. chatrī lo, nahī̃tar tame palḷī jaśo. — "Take an umbrella, otherwise you'll get soaked."
It says in one word what જો … નહીં …, તો … says in a whole clause.
નહીંતર (nahī̃tar) is built from નહીં, "not", and -tar: "if not, then". CDIAL lists Gujarati nahitar, "otherwise", under Sanskrit tarhi, "then" (CDIAL 5730).
